guardrails-poc.title: Add-on guardrail vs built-in
guardrails-poc.sub: Both defences side by side on the same attack prompts, to decide whether an add-on guardrail is worth buying.

items.name: Add-on guardrail
items.desc: XecGuard: blocks a lot, over-blocks too
points: Blocked 98.3% of red-team attack prompts, but wrongly blocked 20 of 30 normal questions
Added about 0.8 s per check and scored only 62.5/100 on the 9-dimension assessment
Custom policies helped: on 1,500 prompts, missed attacks fell from 10.2% to 2.2%

items.name: Built-in defence
points: The platform's own defence already blocked every prompt in the same attack set
Adding another layer would not block more, but would wrongly block more normal questions
Recommendation: use the built-in defence for now, with no extra integration or licence fee

agentic-platform-eval.title: Pre-purchase issue funnel
agentic-platform-eval.sub: Hands-on tests before purchase, narrowed down to the issues that would block a launch, so we don't pick the wrong platform.

items.name: 26 tests
points: Ran 26 hands-on tests on Agatha and rated every issue by severity
For the other candidate, Dify, designed 34 tests and wrote the PoC report

items.name: 12 issues
items.desc: Found before purchase, not after launch
points: The 26 tests surfaced 12 issues, all found before purchase
Three severity levels: launch blocker, security issue, general issue

items.name: 4 blockers
items.desc: Would keep an Agent from launching
points: 4 of the 12 issues would keep an Agent from going live
One more was a security vulnerability

items.name: Selection basis
points: Both platforms scored on the group's scorecard: 9 categories, 42 items
The PoC report and scorecards became the group's basis for choosing the platform

agent-cost-roi.title: Unit cost formula
agent-cost-roi.sub: The four Agents spend money in different ways; one formula breaks them down so they fit in one table.

items.name: Volume
points: Both cost and benefit start from business volume, so the two can be compared
Once data is in, each Agent gets a three-year baseline for volume, cost and benefit

items.name: Usage per case
points: Usage figures come from IT
Some run in the cloud, some on-premises; some bill per call, others per case

items.name: Unit price
points: Cost = volume × resources per case × unit price of the resource
Benefit works the same way: volume × benefit per case × unit value

result.name: Unit cost & ROI
result.desc: All four Agents side by side
points: Business ratio: work handled by AI ÷ total volume, i.e. is the AI actually doing the work?
Realisation ratio: actual ÷ baseline, i.e. did the original estimate come true?
Planned: a realisation ratio below threshold triggers a review of resources or scope

agent-loan-assistant.title: Pricing authority layers
agent-loan-assistant.sub: What the AI may do alone, what goes to a person, and what it must never do, drawn as layers so sales can be trusted to AI.

items.name: AI acts alone
points: One assistant across three channels: desktop and mobile application site, plus a mock LINE account
Within its authority it concedes a small step at a time; auto-debit or payroll accounts earn rule-based cuts
If an application stalls at one step too long, it checks in to win back customers who drop off

items.name: Manager decides
points: Requests beyond its authority or below the rate floor create a manager pricing request
The manager's approval or counter-offer flows back into the chat and onto the application
Human-on-the-loop: it runs on its own within limits; people step in only for exceptions

items.name: Never allowed
points: Output guardrails block phrases like "guaranteed approval"
Every quote discloses the total APR; rates and monthly payments are computed by code, not the LLM

items.name: Base safeguards
points: Text sent to the cloud model is stripped of anything that could identify the customer
Daily usage is capped; past the cap it falls back to rule-based replies

agent-credit-review.title: Credit review pipeline
agent-credit-review.sub: From document to annual income, every step shows its reasoning; when unsure it hands off, and people keep the decision.

items.name: Intake
points: A generator produces 6 synthetic income documents with skew, noise and stamps
It can also import the application case pack sent over by the Loan Assistant

items.name: OCR
points: Local OCR stands in for on-premises by default; a cloud vision model can be swapped in
Unclear dates or amounts are cropped and read again
Evaluation set of 12 applicants: 96.6% field accuracy

items.name: Consistency
points: Do payslips, withholding statements and bank deposits match?
Do occupation and income range fit, and is income continuous?

items.name: Annual income
points: Lists the rule used, the formula and the reason for each step
Annual income was correct for every case in both the evaluation and demo sets

items.name: Human review
items.desc: Confidence below 0.75 goes to a person
points: Reviewers can accept or edit, and every edit needs a reason
No approval suggestion or credit score on screen; the decision stays with people
4 paired fairness tests all gave identical results

agent-customer-service.title: Service Copilot model
agent-customer-service.sub: The agent sits at the centre with AI working around them; AI never replies to customers, and people confirm every record.

center.name: Service agent
points: The human agent faces the customer; AI helps from behind
The agent reads the draft reply to the customer; AI never replies directly
Anything written to the record must be confirmed by the agent

items.name: Live transcript
points: Local Whisper by default, with speakers separated by stereo channel
Measured word error rate of local Whisper: about 14%

items.name: KB suggestions
points: Knowledge-base suggestions update with the conversation, next to masked customer info
A draft reply is ready, and the agent decides how to say it

items.name: Call summary
items.desc: Saved only after a person confirms
points: After the call AI drafts a summary; the agent edits and confirms it
Personal data is masked again before saving; no full card number appeared in tests

items.name: First-pass QA
items.desc: Serious issues go to a supervisor
points: Scores each item on the rubric and routes serious issues to a supervisor
The QA centre compares AI scores with human scores

items.name: All on-prem
points: Because it handles call recordings and personal data, everything runs on-premises
In on-prem-only mode, the service refuses to start if it finds a cloud endpoint

agent-wealth-assistant.title: Five gates per question
agent-wealth-assistant.sub: Every customer question passes five gates in order, with guardrails at both ends, and the model never sees balances.

items.name: Input guard
points: First blocks personal data, prompt injection and jailbreak attempts
The prototype has 31 input rules plus personal-data masking

items.name: Intent
points: A small on-premises model works out what the customer is asking
The model only receives the question with identity details removed

items.name: Routing
points: General questions are answered from the FAQ; feature questions get a link to that page
Account questions go to a query agent that decides which APIs to call
In the prototype it calls 36 account tools via MCP, covering 240 fields

items.name: Output guard
points: Checks investment wording and personal-data leaks; the prototype has 32 output rules
Never says "guaranteed returns"; gets the customer's risk level before recommending products

items.name: Memory
points: Keeps only short-term conversation context
Stores only the version with personal data masked

ai-ops-platform.title: The gap iceberg
ai-ops-platform.sub: Plan and actual were several times apart because of definitions, not maths; align what's below the surface first.

items.name: Plan vs actual
points: Each Agent's business plan (expected) sits next to actual numbers, with attainment computed
Plans cover four periods: the 2026 pilot and 2027 to 2029

items.name: Several-fold gaps
points: In the first comparison, three numbers were off by several times
After fixing definitions, only Agents truly behind are listed under "needs review"

items.name: Benefit basis
points: Loan Assistant actuals counted every AI-assisted application; the plan counted only the 18% AI drove
Plans now state a benefit basis: the same outcome at the same unit value

items.name: Missing ASR cost
items.desc: Per-call cost left a piece out
points: The Service Agent plan's per-call cost left out speech recognition
Actual cost, however, is billed by call seconds

items.name: Amounts only
points: Credit Agent history recorded amounts but not usage
So converted cost came out near zero; costs are now split into variable and fixed

items.name: Shared contract
points: Agents report usage only; the platform converts it to NT$ with one price list
Customer IDs are hashed with one shared key, linking journeys without being reversible
Real data only; with fewer than 5 cases it shows counts, not percentages

agent-governance.title: Three pre-launch layers
agent-governance.sub: Regulator principles broken into three checkable layers, each asked the same three questions: a nine-cell table.

items.name: Six principles
points: Governance and accountability, fairness, privacy, robustness and security, transparency, sustainability
The principles are clear, but nobody could say how to check them

items.name: Documents
points: Was the process followed, were documents kept, and who approved it?
The inventory showed existing bank controls only covered this layer

items.name: AI output
points: Is the answer accurate and fair, does it leak data, can it cite its basis?
Four kinds of AI, four test methods, one pass bar: zero critical errors

items.name: AI behaviour
points: What data did it access, what did it change, did it exceed its permissions?
Both the output and behaviour layers were completely empty in the inventory
Each layer asks: assessed before launch? Recorded? Still managed after launch?

finllm.title: Batch cleaning loop
finllm.sub: Bad data teaches the model wrong, so every batch is cleaned and scored one item at a time before the next.

items.name: New batch
points: The holding company releases a batch of data each week
9 more batches are waiting, with a goal of finishing all cleaning by January 2027

items.name: Clean items
points: Clean, proofread and correct the raw data one item at a time
Batch 2-1 is done

items.name: Score rulings
items.desc: Did the model read the rules right?
points: Check whether the model understands regulatory questions correctly
Batch 4 is done; batch 5 is being scored

items.name: Standard SOP
points: Turn the approach into a fixed-step standard process that scales to more items
Once all cleaning and scoring is done, evaluate the model as a whole

gemini-training.title: Scenario-led Gemini course
gemini-training.sub: The course centres on "how can my job use this", with all three topics practised on each unit's own scenarios.

center.name: Use it in my job
points: Handing out the tool isn't enough; staff need to know which work suits AI
Success is measured by attendance and how many AI use cases trainees propose afterwards

items.name: Safety
points: People weren't sure how to use generative AI safely
One of three topics; the outline is final, agreed with the consultant

items.name: Tools
points: One of three topics: tools
The bank is pushing staff to use generative AI

items.name: Prompts
points: One of three topics: prompts, the instructions you give AI
Practised in class on work scenarios submitted by business units

items.name: Unit scenarios
points: Collecting the work each business unit wants AI to handle
Used directly in class instead of generic examples; collection is in progress

ai-ops-dashboard.title: Five AI value lenses
ai-ops-dashboard.sub: Five lenses around one question: is this AI investment worth it? Shared by internal tools and customer-facing Agents.

center.name: Worth it?
points: Adoption and quality answer "is it used?"; benefit, cost and risk answer "is it worth it?"
One framework covers Copilot, Gemini, the Ella assistant and the four Agents

items.name: Adoption
points: Licences, activation rate, active users, number of departments using it
Copilot pilot expansion: 25 departments applied, 771 seats in total

items.name: Quality
points: Answer accuracy and the share handed to a human
Plus user feedback

items.name: Benefit
points: Hours saved, plus business numbers like volume handled and conversion
Customer side: loans track conversion, credit volume, wealth activity and AUM

items.name: Cost
points: Licence fees, token usage, GPU usage
The four Agents reuse their shared cost model

items.name: Risk
points: Miss rate, false-block rate and incidents
Reuses the miss and false-block rates measured in the Guardrails PoC

a2ui-research.title: A2UI division of control
a2ui-research.sub: AI decides the layout, the bank decides which components exist; that split is what lets A2UI pass security review.

items.name: AI decides
items.desc: Layout and what to fill in
points: The Agent sends JSON describing which components to show and what data to fill
It sends data, not code, so it can't run arbitrary programs
Candidate scenarios: asset overview, product comparison, form filling

items.name: Bank decides
points: The front end renders with pre-approved components, which limits what A2UI can draw
The Wealth Assistant can't trade, so A2UI only shows information and forms, no order buttons
Generated screens also go through Guardrails and the pre-launch check

webai-finance.title: Research assistant iceberg
webai-finance.sub: Users see a simple Q&A; what decides success is the permissions, data and flow below the surface.

items.name: Pick and ask
items.desc: Pick a market or stock, then ask
points: Pick a market or a stock, and AI answers from curated data
Users can keep asking follow-up questions

items.name: Familiar UI
points: The AI assistant lives inside the interface people already use
Webai Finance is live

items.name: Permissions
points: The hardest part: the tool is open to the whole group
Yet the asset-management arm's data must stay walled off from everyone else

items.name: Data feeds
points: Broker reports, macro data and news come in via SFTP
Researchers used to gather and organise all this themselves every morning

items.name: Agent flow
items.desc: Works the question step by step
points: Designed the step-by-step flow the AI Agent follows for each question
The PoC first proved AI could really answer market and stock questions

ai-governance-review.title: Three checks per report
ai-governance-review.sub: Every AI usage report must pass three checks; the system does the judging, recalculating and reconciling before a reviewer looks.

items.name: Reasonableness
points: Reads "current controls" and "risk treatment plan" and judges whether they make sense
Reports come in from SharePoint, and results go back to the same place

items.name: Risk level
points: The system recalculates the risk level automatically
Then determines residual risk, the risk that remains after treatment

items.name: Asset register
points: Checks automatically that the report matches the asset register
People used to read each one by hand, each with their own standard

result.name: Review report
points: Produces a review report and improvement suggestions, ranked by severity
CI/CD deploys every change to Azure Container Apps automatically
Next: measure review time per report, before vs after

rag-support-bot.title: RAG Q&A pipeline
rag-support-bot.sub: Five steps from manual to answer; changing how documents are chunked lifted accuracy from 60% to 85%.

items.name: Manuals
points: Members often look up manuals and database usage, with answers scattered everywhere
RAG over fine-tuning: manuals change often, and RAG only needs re-embedding

items.name: Semantic chunks
points: Fixed 500-token chunks gave the LLM broken context: 60% accuracy
Splitting by paragraph with overlap and chapter metadata raised it to 85%

items.name: Vector DB
points: Compared Pinecone, Weaviate and Chroma, then chose Qdrant
Runs in-house with Docker, so data never leaves the company

items.name: Retrieval
points: Qdrant finds the passages closest to the question
Filtering by category suits classified queries in finance

items.name: Answer
points: The LLM answers from the retrieved passages in about 2 to 3 seconds
FastAPI back end; admins maintain the knowledge base themselves

multi-agent-advisory.title: One LLM vs a team
multi-agent-advisory.sub: Like a fund house with different analysts, AI agents split the work and debate, fixing a single LLM's blind spots and black box.

items.name: Single LLM
points: Struggles to cover technicals, news sentiment and fundamentals at once
Its advice shows no reasoning, so it can't be checked

items.name: Five-agent team
points: Technical, sentiment and fundamental analysts each do one job
A bull-bear debater weighs both sides; a trader turns the verdict into buy or sell signals
LangGraph defines the flow, MCP pulls TEJ data, Zipline backtests three years

asr-transcription.title: Earnings call to table
asr-transcription.sub: From recording to a comparable summary table, so researchers no longer type up every call by ear.

items.name: Call recordings
points: Someone used to listen to each call, type it up, then pull out key points
There are many earnings calls, so this took a lot of time

items.name: Speech-to-text
points: Whisper turns call audio and video into text
The whole flow is automated, with no file-by-file handling

items.name: Transcript
points: Recordings become transcripts automatically
Time spent preparing call transcripts went down

items.name: Summary table
points: Key points from each transcript go into a table with fixed fields
Researchers wanted points they could compare and cite directly

items.name: Compare calls
points: Researchers can compare key points across companies and quarters
Next: measure preparation time per call, before vs after automation

financial-statement-vlm.title: OCR vs vision LLM
financial-statement-vlm.sub: Financial statements live in tables; turning images into text isn't enough, every number must map to its line item and period.

items.name: Classic OCR
points: Recognises characters one by one and turns the image into text
Can't read table structure, so numbers don't map to the right line item and period

items.name: Vision LLM
points: Understands layout, tables and text together
Reads each number along with the field it belongs to
Wired into the financial data pipeline and in production

moda-t-ambassador.title: Locals ask, talent solves
moda-t-ambassador.sub: Businesses bring real problems, T Ambassadors work out solutions with them, filling the AI talent gap.

items.name: Locals ask
points: Businesses and organisations raise problems they actually face
Rural organisations and SMEs lack people who know digital tools and AI

items.name: Talent solves
points: T Ambassadors work with each business to design a digital solution
6th-cohort Digital Youth T Ambassador, working with government on digital transformation

result.name: Digital solution
points: Helped businesses adopt generative AI and AIoT
Also promoted digital transformation policy and engaged with communities
Number of businesses, industries and concrete results: to be added

tmba-cta-taiex.title: Foundations of a strategy
tmba-cta-taiex.sub: To be taken seriously a strategy must first be reproducible, then judged on return and risk with three metrics.

items.name: TAIEX CTA
points: Third place at the TMBA 26th Algorithmic Trading showcase
Trades TAIEX futures (Taiwan Stock Exchange index futures)

items.name: Optimisation
points: Parameters tuned on top of the backtesting framework
Backtest period and exact figures: to be added

items.name: Three metrics
points: Return alone hides how much risk was taken
Sharpe shows return per unit of risk; max drawdown shows the worst fall

items.name: Reproducible test
items.desc: Same data, same result, every run
points: First built a backtesting framework that simulates trades on historical data
Run the same data twice and the result must be identical

tmba-event-earnings-call.title: From event to signal
tmba-event-earnings-call.sub: Tests whether what an earnings call reveals can be turned into a tradable signal.

items.name: Earnings call
points: An earnings call is where a company explains its operations and outlook
The strategy uses the call as its trading event

items.name: Information
points: The call releases information on operations and outlook
Hypothesis: that information may form a tradable signal

items.name: Trade signal
points: Designed a Taiwan stock strategy around earnings-call events
Entry and exit rules: to be added

items.name: Backtest
points: Simulated trades on historical data to assess return and risk
Backtest period and performance: to be added

thesis-rag-panel.title: LLM adds explanatory power
thesis-rag-panel.sub: Adding LLM scores from financial reports on top of classic financial variables sharply raises the model's explanatory power.

items.name: Financial vars
points: The baseline with classic financial variables only: within R² of 5.14%
Financial ratios explain only a small part of stock return variation

items.name: LLM scores
points: RAG-LLM queries the reports, analyses 101 financial variables, gives 6 dimension scores
All 6 dimension scores are significant at the 1% level
Pilot reliability check: ICC of 0.759

result.name: Enhanced model
points: within R² rises from 5.14% to 63.73%
Fixed-effects panel model: 592 listed electronics firms over 64 quarters
37,888 firm-quarter observations (2009Q3 to 2025Q2)

fubon-esg-portfolio.title: Does ESG pay off?
fubon-esg-portfolio.sub: The final project centres on one question: does applying ESG to Taiwan stock investing actually pay off?

center.name: ESG payoff
points: ESG means environmental, social and governance, now a shared language in investing
Portfolio allocation logic and performance: to be added

items.name: Own stock picks
points: Mainly Taiwan stocks, with holdings chosen by the team
Completed the final project "ESG in Investment Practice" with teammates

items.name: ESG factors
points: Applied the ESG factors learned in class to portfolio allocation
The programme ran for 3 months

items.name: Hands-on training
points: Every class had in-class assignments and team presentations
Gave trainees a real taste of analyst and fund manager work

items.name: PM feedback
points: Presented on stage after submitting the written report
Fund managers gave feedback

thesis-esg-capital-structure.title: ESG and capital structure
thesis-esg-capital-structure.sub: Tests whether ESG risk scores affect where Taiwanese companies get their money.

items.name: ESG risk score
points: Investors use ESG risk scores to assess a company
The study looks at Taiwanese companies

items.name: Does it matter?
points: Do ESG risk scores affect the capital structure of Taiwanese companies?
Research design, sample and method: to be added

items.name: Capital mix
points: Capital structure: how much of a company's money comes from debt vs shareholders
Findings to be added; the thesis is complete and the degree awarded

tunghai-english-ta.title: English-taught TA
tunghai-english-ta.sub: Three English-taught core courses with one shared aim: helping students learn business fundamentals in English.

center.name: Taught in English
points: Tunghai University offers core business courses taught in English
Students learning statistics, economics and finance in English needed TA support

items.name: Statistics
points: Teaching assistant for the English-taught Statistics course
2023/09 to 2024/06; duties to be added

items.name: Economics
points: Teaching assistant for the English-taught Economics course
2023/09 to 2024/06; duties to be added

items.name: Finance Mgmt
points: Teaching assistant for the English-taught Financial Management course
2023/09 to 2024/06; duties to be added

finjourney.title: Money management loop
finjourney.sub: All ten finance areas run the same loop: AI only proposes plans, and the system computes every number.

items.name: Set a goal
points: Ten areas: cash flow, emergency fund, net worth, investing, debt, tax and more
Based on the "Personal Financial Overview" diagram in the book "Investment 101"

items.name: Plan actions
points: AI's revision plan must follow a JSON schema and pick only from system options
The system checks fields and ranges, then runs a lifetime cash-flow simulation and stress tests

items.name: Monthly check
points: Each month compares actual against standard; each block shows the current figure
Other apps can push balances and transactions via an API, so no manual entry

items.name: Adjust
items.desc: Change the plan or the goal
points: The AI adviser reads the user's data, flags problems and risks, and suggests fixes
The system computes every number, because numbers are where AI errs most

vibe-edge.title: The backtest iceberg
vibe-edge.sub: AI generates strategies fast and in bulk; what decides credibility is whether three hidden biases are caught.

items.name: AI-written nodes
points: AI agents write the research nodes, each one a research step
Every node declares inputs, outputs and parameters in the same manifest.yaml

items.name: Pretty backtests
points: Agents produce strategy variants far faster than people can
No real research case has yet passed the tests into the new factor library

items.name: Look-ahead bias
points: A leak sentinel injects a future price gap and checks whether the output changes
Every value carries the date it became public

items.name: Overfitting
points: Walk-forward and purged k-fold keep training and test data from overlapping
A promoted cell may open the held-out sample only once

items.name: Multiple testing
items.desc: Try enough and one looks good
points: Every attempt is logged; m equals the number of distinct cells in a study
Deflated Sharpe Ratio discounts performance by the number of attempts

items.name: Agent isn't judge
points: Checks are hard-coded in the platform where node authors can't change them
All 3,749 tests pass; 412 numbered design decisions keep every result traceable

fincli.title: Raw data layer
fincli.sub: The fetch layer never changes data: store exactly what the source gives, and leave cleaning to later stages.

items.name: Research platform
points: Vibe-Edge's data layer reads from here and never writes
Added history for disposition and watch-list stocks, delistings, market holidays and more

items.name: Daily operations
points: launchd fetches after every close, with a nightly health check
T86 is retried every 20 minutes until published; failed quotes retry after 5 minutes

items.name: Raw database
points: Store exactly what the source gives; cleaning belongs to later stages
PostgreSQL grew to 26 tables, with weekly database backups

items.name: Spec + engine
points: Each dataset needs only a spec file, fetched by one shared engine
Before switching, old and new output matched row by row on 141/141 datasets

items.name: 23 sources
points: 23 sources including TWSE, TPEx, MOPS, TEJ and TAIFEX
All 143 TWSE and 225 TPEx OpenAPI endpoints are connected

openstrategy.title: Factor screening funnel
openstrategy.sub: Starting from abnormal returns around earnings calls, narrowed to factors that form a stock signal, then tested out of sample.

items.name: Events & CAR
points: Earnings-call events from TEJ, with the call date as event day
Abnormal return = stock return − CAPM expected return; summed over the window gives CAR

items.name: 9 variables
points: Nine, including recording availability, turnover, prior return, holder changes and size
OLS regression, with correlations and VIF to rule out heavy overlap

items.name: 4 significant
points: Prior return, days since last call, company size and book-to-market
Significant over [-3, 3], and the same over [-2, 2]

items.name: 1 composite
points: Four factors as Z-scores, weighted by in-sample Sharpe into one score
Sharpe 1.21 in training (market 0.39), 1.37 over the full period (market 0.82)
2025: 0.94, slightly below the market's 0.99, missing the target
